ÉTOILE KSA ✦ THE BRAND SAVER'S CREATIVE MISSIONS
هلا بايتس
A Month-Long Campaign
Cultural Localization & Creative Strategy

From an Egyptian seasonal tradition to a potential new Saudi consumption habit.

01 / The briefSTRATEGY FILE

THE CHALLENGE

How do you introduce traditional Egyptian Mawlid sweets to Saudi consumers who don't necessarily share the same cultural connection to the occasion?

The campaign was planned to run for an entire month. Rather than repeating one creative angle throughout, I needed to sustain interest by introducing different reasons to discover, try, and enjoy the products.

The bigger challenge was to move beyond selling an Egyptian seasonal specialty and explore how it could become part of familiar Saudi consumption habits.

✦
02 / Consumer understandingSTRATEGY FILE

THE STRATEGIC INSIGHT

To introduce a new product tradition, you need more than one reason to embrace it.

Saudi consumers might not connect with the Egyptian Mawlid occasion itself, but they could connect with the products through culturally familiar moments: welcoming guests, family gatherings, sharing sweets with coffee, and treating loved ones.

Other motivations, such as convenient snacking and limited seasonal availability, could create additional reasons to try the products.

Instead of relying on one cultural message for an entire month, I saw an opportunity to build multiple entry points into the same product experience.

✦
03 / Concept platformSTRATEGY FILE

MY CREATIVE MOVE

One campaign platform. Multiple concepts. Different motivations.

I developed هلا بايتس as the umbrella creative concept, combining the familiar Saudi greeting «هلا» with the modern, bite-sized appeal of the products.

Rather than stretching one execution across the entire month, I structured the campaign around several complementary creative directions, each serving a different strategic purpose:

✦
04 / Five strategic directions1—2 / 5

THE CREATIVE DIRECTIONS

1.

هلا بالأحبة | Cultural Connection

Positioning traditional Egyptian sweets as a welcoming gesture for guests and loved ones, tapping into Saudi hospitality and social gatherings.

2.

Paired بلذاذة! | Habit Integration

Connecting the sweets with coffee culture, using playful Bluetooth-pairing wordplay to introduce them as a natural companion to an established daily ritual.

✦
05 / Five strategic directions3—5 / 5

THE CREATIVE DIRECTIONS

3.

Energy Bites | New Usage Occasions

Reframing selected products as convenient, bite-sized snacks for busy and active moments, expanding their relevance beyond traditional celebrations.

4.

أيام حلاها غير | Seasonal Appeal

Using limited seasonal availability to create curiosity and a reason to try the products before they disappear.

5.

منمنمات الحلا | Product Reframing

Highlighting the smaller format of the sweets to make them feel more versatile, contemporary, and easier to incorporate into different moments throughout the day.

✦
06 / Month-long architectureSTRATEGY FILE

THE CONTENT STRATEGY

I designed a month-long content approach that rotated between different creative concepts, cultural connections, and purchase motivations.

Each direction gave the audience a fresh perspective on the same products while maintaining a consistent campaign identity.

The strategy balanced:

Cultural relevance: Connecting the products to Saudi hospitality, gatherings, and coffee rituals.
Habit creation: Encouraging consumers to discover new occasions for enjoying traditional Egyptian sweets.
Creative variety: Keeping the month-long campaign engaging through different concepts rather than repetitive executions.
✦
07 / Strategic balance continuedTHE BALANCE

THE CONTENT STRATEGY

Product repositioning: Introducing the sweets as versatile treats beyond their original seasonal context.
Commercial motivation: Combining emotional appeal, product discovery, convenience, and limited-time availability.

Together, these layers helped the campaign stay culturally relevant, commercially engaging, and strategically fresh throughout the month.

✦
08 / The strategic valueSTRATEGY FILE

THE STRATEGIC VALUE

I wasn't simply adapting an Egyptian campaign for Saudi Arabia. I was exploring how an Egyptian tradition could find a new place in Saudi consumers' lives.

By developing multiple creative directions under one campaign platform, I aimed to introduce the products through different cultural and commercial motivations, sustain interest throughout the month, and encourage consumption beyond the original Egyptian occasion.

The objective wasn't just to make the products culturally acceptable. It was to create opportunities for them to become familiar, desirable, and potentially part of new consumption habits.
